feedback.problem: Determine the horizontal asymptote of the function $f(x)=\frac{2{x}^{2}+3}{8{x}^{5}+x-1}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
To find the horizontal asymptote of a rational function, we divide every term in the numerator and denominator by the dominant term in the denominator, and then we let $x\to \infty .$

Ignoring the coefficient, the dominant term in the denominator is ${x}^{5}.$ So, we divide every term in the numerator and denominator by ${x}^{5},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{2{x}^{2}+3}{8{x}^{5}+x-1} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{2{x}^{2}}{{x}^{5}}+\frac{3}{{x}^{5}})}{(\frac{8{x}^{5}}{{x}^{5}}+\frac{x}{{x}^{5}}-\frac{1}{{x}^{5}})} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{2}{{x}^{3}}+\frac{3}{{x}^{5}})}{(8+\frac{1}{{x}^{4}}-\frac{1}{{x}^{5}})}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, when $x$ is very large, the terms $\frac{2}{{x}^{3}},\frac{3}{{x}^{5}},\frac{1}{{x}^{4}}$ and $\frac{1}{{x}^{5}}$ become very small. Therefore, as $x\to \infty ,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{(\frac{2}{{x}^{3}}+\frac{3}{{x}^{5}})}{(8+\frac{1}{{x}^{4}}-\frac{1}{{x}^{5}})} \\  & \to \frac{0+0}{8+0-0} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the horizontal asymptote is $y=0.$
